STEP 1 - Scene: A single plated meal, a white square plate on a glass table, photographed from above at a slight angle. It shows a piece of pan-fried or roasted meat (pork or chicken, with crispy golden skin on top) next to a pile of mixed salad leaves (rocket/arugula-like greens with thin red-stemmed leaves and sliced onion).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square dinner-style plate about 26 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 26 x 26 ≈ 530 cm² (square plate, so using side length directly).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roasted/pan-fried meat with crispy skin (pulled/shredded pieces, likely pork or chicken thigh)
- Mixed salad leaves (rocket/arugula, mustard-type greens, red-stemmed leaves)
- Thin sliced onion/shallot pieces mixed with the leaves

STEP 4 - Area:
- Meat with crispy skin: ~22% of plate (about 115 cm²)
- Salad leaves: ~20% of plate (about 105 cm²)
- Onion slivers: ~2% (about 10 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 44% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Meat: 115 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 290 ml
- Salad: 105 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 315 ml
- Onion: 10 cm² x 1 cm ≈ 10 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Meat: 290 ml x 0.9 ≈ 260 g
- Salad: 315 ml x 0.15 ≈ 47 g
- Onion: 10 ml x 0.6 ≈ 6 g

STEP 7 - Energy (cooked weight):
- Roast meat with skin (pork/chicken mix): 260 g x 230 kcal/100g ≈ 598 kcal. Pork/chicken with skin averages roughly 200–250 kcal/100g; I use 230.
- Salad leaves: 47 g x 25 kcal/100g ≈ 12 kcal
- Onion: 6 g x 40 kcal/100g ≈ 2 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A moderate portion of meat and a side salad on a dinner plate totaling about 310 g and roughly 610 kcal is plausible. The meat portion is fairly generous, so the estimate may run high; the true total is likely in the 450–650 kcal range.
